pool.text: Spanish explorer Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo claimed the area of southern California for his empire.
A group of forty-four settlers known as Los Pobladores founded the pueblo of Los Angeles.
The settlement became part of the First Mexican Empire following the war of independence.
Los Angeles was officially incorporated as a municipality months before achieving statehood.
Railroads arrived in the city with the completion of the Southern Pacific line.
Petroleum was discovered in the city and surrounding area, sparking major industrial growth.
The city hosted the Summer Olympics for the first time in its history.
The largest passenger rail terminal in the Western United States opened.
Racial tensions led to the Watts riots, resulting in dozens of deaths.
California became the birthplace of the Internet with the first ARPANET transmission.
Tom Bradley was elected as the municipality's first African American mayor.
The city hosted the Summer Olympic Games for a second time.
Racial tensions erupted into large-scale riots following a controversial police jury verdict.
A magnitude earthquake shook the municipality, causing widespread damage and deaths.
Voters ratified a current municipal charter that created neighborhood councils.
Voters defeated efforts by the San Fernando Valley and Hollywood to secede.
Los Angeles workers had a mean travel time for work commutes.
Both ports achieved a massive trade volume of container units.
The municipality successfully met its goal of providing power from renewable sources.
The World Cruise Center served a large number of passengers.
